owners.reason: The platform leaf owns real filesystem, process, executable, IPC, and host-resource mechanics selected for each native target.
Broker integration tests exercise native process identity, singleton leases, IPC routes, kill semantics, and executable replacement.
Daemon integration tests exercise native process lifetime, IPC, file-backed state, restart, stall, and cache-maintenance behavior.
Front-door integration tests launch target-native soldr, cargo, rustc, compiler wrappers, linkers, and trampolines.
Cache and GC integration tests exercise native filesystem traversal, deletion, locking, worktree discovery, and disk policy.
Cook and Dylint integration tests execute native build tools and exchange materialized artifacts with the daemon.
Tool integration tests execute downloaded or embedded target-native binaries and validate host archive and executable behavior.
Toolchain and environment integration tests exercise native discovery, shims, process environments, archives, and host tooling.
The integration test validates executable-mode preservation through the host filesystem and archive implementation.
The integration test validates target-native Windows named-pipe peer identity and attribution.
The integration tests exercise native link, permission, executable, and child-process behavior around the embedded compiler service.
The target-native executable contract catches host environment representation and process-launch regressions.
